To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the binding free energies of CsA and a set of its analogs, modeled in complexes with the cyclophilin of T. cruzi, did not correlate with the experimental data, probably due to the existence of multiple binding sites.

the LIE method was not suitable for the calculation of binding free energies of the complexes of TcCyP with CsA and analogs, and that molecular docking identified alternative binding sites with similar energies to the active binding site.

1) the binding free energy values obtained with the LIE method did not correlate with the experimental data; 2) the docking calculations identified three possible binding sites, two of them with comparable scores to the active site; 3) further MD studies are required to confirm the multiple binding sites and/or to find a better correlation with experimental data.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new inhibitors of the TcCyP, which could become new leads for the design of antiparasitic drugs.
the development of new inhibitors for TcCyP and the identification of new binding sites.
the development of new inhibitors of TcCyP as a potential target for the treatment of Chagas disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the LIE method is not applicable to these systems, and that the binding sites found in the docking calculations should be further explored by other computational methods.
, in spite of the limitations found in our study, the molecular modeling of CsA analogs in TcCyP 19 complexes is a promising approach to find new trypanocidal compounds.
the LIE method is not applicable for this set of ligands.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the LIE method is not a good option to compute binding free energy in the case of the modeled TcCyP/CsA complexes, and that further studies are required to identify a more appropriate method.

, although we were not able to obtain good correlations between binding free energies and experimental data, the results obtained are useful for the identification of the most important interactions and residues involved in the inhibition of the enzyme by the compounds, as well as for the identification of other putative binding regions that could be explored in future experiments.
, although the LIE method was not able to predict the experimental binding free energies, the MD calculations were able to identify other putative binding pockets for CsA and analogs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the binding free energy analysis of the modeled complexes is not conclusive.
the application of the docking-LIE method for the study of TcCyP is not straightforward.
the application of LIE to the TcCyP-CsA analogs systems is not recommended.
